headline: FDA Clears Maggot Therapy for Wound Care, 2nd Species Approved
summary: The FDA has cleared a second species of fly for maggot therapy, a treatment that uses live maggots to clean wounds. This therapy is used to promote healing.
details: The FDA has cleared a second species of fly for maggot therapy, a treatment that uses live maggots to clean wounds. This therapy is used to promote healing.
Maggot therapy, also known as maggot debridement therapy, involves the use of live maggots to clean wounds by breaking down dead tissue.
The first species of fly to be cleared for this therapy was the common green bottle fly. The newly cleared species is another type of fly that has been found to be effective in wound care.

FDA clears 2nd species for maggot wound therapy - what makes this unusual treatment effective?

The FDA has cleared a second species of fly for maggot therapy, a treatment that uses live maggots to clean wounds. This therapy is used to promote healing.

Maggot therapy, also known as maggot debridement therapy, involves the use of live maggots to clean wounds by breaking down dead tissue.

The first species of fly to be cleared for this therapy was the common green bottle fly. The newly cleared species is another type of fly that has been found to be effective in wound care.
